In 1672 the Danish West India Company settled St Thomas, beginning the Danish West Indies. Denmark added St John in 1718 and bought St Croix from France in 1733.

St Thomas, with its port of Charlotte Amalie, became a free port and a busy hub of trade, while St John and St Croix were covered in sugar estates. Enslaved Africans, shipped in Danish vessels from the Gold Coast, made up most of the people.

Denmark banned its slave trade from 1803, among the first nations to do so, but slavery lasted until the emancipation of 1848. The islands declined with sugar and were sold to the United States in 1917. Danish street names and buildings remain.
